samples.question: This image shows a row of balloons drawn on white paper. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. Each balloon is one solid coloured oval, and under every balloon exactly one straight dark grey STRING hangs downwards. A string is TIED when its top end touches the bottom of its balloon, and it is LOOSE when a clear band of white paper, at least ten pixels tall, separates the top end of the string from the bottom of the balloon. Every balloon has its own string and all the strings are the same length, so the amount of dark ink is the same however many strings are loose. The number of balloons, their colours, their sizes, their heights on the page and which balloons carry the loose strings all change from image to image. Judge only what is painted in this image, and do not answer from the fact that balloons are normally tied to their strings. How many of the strings are loose? Answer with exactly one of the integers 0, 1, 2, or 3.
